questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical CKAD tasks around StatefulSets, per-pod storage, and graceful upgrades.

## Key Concepts

- StatefulSet and VolumeClaimTemplates
- Headless service and stable network identity
- Update strategy and partitioning
- Termination behavior and preStop
- PodDisruptionBudget and rollback

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: cache-node
spec:
  serviceName: cache-svc
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cache-node
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cache-node
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cache
        image: your-registry/cache:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test upgrades and rollback?
- How would you ensure data safety during node reschedules?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD ability to compose a small, namespace-scoped verification workflow that touches ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and network policy.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment with InitContainer
- ConfigMap-based allowlist
- Secret-based credentials and TLS sidecar
- PVC-mounted /secrets and lightweight parsing with jq/yq
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default
data:
  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl && wget -O - https://github.com/yq-dev/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/local/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
      containers:
        - name: checker
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./check.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: secrets
              mountPath: /secrets
      volumes:
        - name: secrets
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: secret-storage
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale and test this in a real cluster?
- What are risks with mounting Secrets in /secrets and how to mitigate?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical use of ConfigMaps, envFrom, and volume mounting; checks how changes trigger controlled rollouts with an annotation-based restart cue; covers health checks basics.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments, ConfigMaps, envFrom
- Volumes and ConfigMap mounts
- Rolling restarts via PodTemplate annotations
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- Trade-offs: restart cost vs. up-to-date config, ConfigMap size impacts, security

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConfigMap skeleton
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
data:
  FLAG_A: "true"
  FLAG_B: "false"
---
# Deployment skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: feature-flag-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: feature-flag-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: feature-flag-service
      annotations:
        checksum.feature-flags: "{{ .Values.configMap.checksum }}"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: feature-flags
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /config/flags
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: feature-flags
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **Restart Cost vs. Fresh Config**: Rolling restarts ensure configuration consistency but cause temporary availability reduction
- **ConfigMap Size Impact**: Large ConfigMaps increase annotation length and may affect API server performance
- **Security Considerations**: Environment variables expose config to process inspection; file mounts provide better isolation
- **Update Latency**: Annotation-based restarts are immediate but may be disruptive compared to hot-reload approaches

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of InitContainer lifecycle, idempotent seeding patterns, and persistent cache management across pod restarts.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers and startup ordering
- ConfigMap-based seed script injection
- PVC-backed shared cache for idempotence
- Marker file pattern for preventing re-seeding
- Readiness and liveness probe configuration
- Load testing and rollback strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
# Seed script ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: seed-scripts
data:
  seed.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
    set -e
    if [ ! -f /cache/.seeded ]; then
      # Execute seeding logic here
      touch /cache/.seeded
    fi
---
# Deployment with InitContainer
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
  namespace: ckad
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed-cache
        image: busybox:1.35
        command: ['/bin/sh', '/scripts/seed.sh']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: seed-scripts
          mountPath: /scripts
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache
      containers:
      - name: api-server
        image: api-server:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: seed-scripts
        configMap:
          name: seed-scripts
      - name: cache-volume
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: cache-pvc
```

## Verification Strategy
1. **Load Testing**: Use kubectl exec to simulate concurrent requests, monitor cache seeding behavior, and verify marker file prevents re-seeding
2. **Rollback Approach**: Deploy with strategy type RollingUpdate, set maxUnavailable and maxSurge for controlled rollout, and use kubectl rollout undo if issues arise
3. **Monitoring**: Check InitContainer logs, verify probe status, and confirm cache persistence across pod restarts

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CronJob usage, PVs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, Secrets, probes, and NetworkPolicy in a realistic backup workflow.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling from ConfigMap
- PVC mounts and tar packaging
- InitContainer tooling prep
- Secret-based credentials for remote backups
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy egress controls

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-backup
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: installer
              image: busybox
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - apk add --no-cache tar pigz
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: alpine:3.18
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - tar -czf /backup/namespace-$(date +%F-%H%M).tar.gz -C /data .
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: backup
                  mountPath: /backup
              readinessProbe:
                exec:
                  command:
                    - cat
                    - /tmp/healthy
                initialDelaySeconds: 30
                periodSeconds: 60
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /healthz
                  port: 8080
```

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design production-ready, per-namespace observability data flows—a critical skill for platform engineers and SREs. It tests familiarity with Kubernetes security primitives, resource management, and operational patterns that generic deployments often overlook.

## Key Concepts Tested

- **Per-namespace isolation:** Scoping a Deployment to each namespace ensures data locality and prevents cross-namespace metric contamination.

- **Operational concerns:** Probes, InitContainers, and sidecars reflect real-world operational complexity.

## Common Pitfalls

Candidates often miss NetworkPolicy egress rules, underconfigure resource limits, or overlook the trade-offs between Pushgateway reliability and simplicity. Strong candidates will proactively discuss alternatives like Prometheus scraping or distributed tracing backends.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests real-world container orchestration patterns: InitContainers for bootstrap, sidecar for log shipping, shared volumes for cross-container data, and proper health checks plus rollback strategy.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for pre-boot config
- Shared volumes and proper MountPaths
- Sidecar pattern for log shipping
- Readiness and Liveness probes tailored to production workloads
- Rollback strategy and safe deploys

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal patch sketch
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: processor
  namespace: payments
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: fix-permissions
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/logs"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /mnt/logs
      containers:
      - name: processor
        image: your-registry/processor:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: in-data
          mountPath: /data/input
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log/processor
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "256Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /readyz
            port: 8080
      - name: log-shipper
        image: busybox:stable
        command: ["sh", "-c", "tail -F /var/log/processor/app.log | nc log-collector 10514"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /var/log/processor
        - name: ship
          mountPath: /var/log/ship
      volumes:
      - name: in-data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: processor-input-pvc
      - name: logs
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: ship
        emptyDir: {}
      restartPolicy: Always
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate zero-downtime rollouts with this setup? 
- How would you monitor and retry failed log shipments without impacting processor throughput?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical Kubernetes patching: config-driven behavior, rolling restarts, probes, and safety nets via quota and PDB.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-based feature flags with rolling restarts via checksum/config
- Probes (readiness and liveness) for service health
- Pod lifecycle: preStop grace period
- PodDisruptionBudget for maintenance safety
- Namespace quotas and limits to enforce resource usage

## Code Example
```yaml
# snippet illustrating patch targets
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments
  namespace: bank
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checksum/config: <hash-of-configmap> # computed hash
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: payments
          image: payments:latest
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
            limits:
              cpu: "500m"
              memory: "256Mi"
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /livez
              port: 8080
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["sleep", "5"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: risk-config
              mountPath: /etc/risk
      volumes:
        - name: risk-config
          configMap:
            name: risk-config
---
apiVersion: policy/v1beta1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: payments-pdb
  namespace: bank
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payments
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: bank-quota
  namespace: bank
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "2"
    requests.memory: 4Gi
    limits.cpu: "4"
    limits.memory: 8Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: bank-limits
  namespace: bank
spec:
  limits:
  - max:
      cpu: "1"
      memory: "512Mi"
    min:
      cpu: "50m"
      memory: "64Mi"
    type: Container
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test rolling restart triggered by ConfigMap changes in a live cluster?
- What changes would you make if you need zero-downtime deployments during quota exhaustion?
